finding: [&>*]:h-auto/min-h-8 applied to EVERY child distorts non-default Button sizes (lg 36px->32px; icon-sm/xs no longer square) and leaks padding/min-height onto plain layout children.

Doc claimed the child rules win by SPECIFICITY; both are (0,1,0) and the override actually wins by Tailwind emission order. Reader would draw a wrong conclusion about !important/inline-style children.

Nested nav group received flex-wrap but NOT max-w-full/whitespace-normal: CardActions' rules reach direct children only, so a single over-wide nav label reproduces the original unreachable-overflow defect inside the fix.
justify-between + wrap degenerates: a wrapped line holding ONE item is placed at main-START, so the nav group jumps to the inline-start edge once the row wraps.
min-w-0 on a `truncate` element is a no-op (overflow:hidden already yields automatic-min-size 0) and the comment attributed causal weight to it.
measureReach treated overflow:hidden WITH overflow as user-scrollable, so the END-edge mirror of the defect under test would have measured green. overflow:hidden is not user-scrollable.
TEST-4 asserted DOM order via ascending raw `left`, encoding LTR as an invariant in a repo that mandates direction-agnostic UI.

After wrapping, 'Approve for this conversation' renders as a full-width, filled, ~2-line button while Deny stays 81x32 outline: relative prominence on the consent surface now favours the broadest approval. No test guards relative prominence.
TEST-8 accepted a tool name CSS-truncated to 60px; the name is attacker-controlled, and a truncated name is misleading rather than merely less legible.
flex-wrap lets an unbounded, nowrap, attacker-supplied server label take a whole line and displace the authentic '— needs approval' status onto another.
Target-size asymmetry favours the risky action: Deny stays 81x32 (below the taxonomy G5 44px mobile floor) while the broadest approval becomes ~238x48.
whitespace-normal without text-center gives a wrapped 2-line label ragged inline-start lines inside a flex-centred button.
CardActionsProps does not require data-testid, diverging from CardProps/ButtonProps; tests must select on a raw [data-slot] attribute outside the testid registry.
TEST-5 was paper coverage: the elicitation footer (~146px of a ~238px row) never overflowed at 390px, so every reachability assertion passed identically on the pre-fix markup.
TEST-3/TEST-4 compared viewport-relative `top` values sampled across separate scrollIntoViewIfNeeded calls; scroll drift could make an unwrapped row look wrapped (and vice versa).
gotoUntilVisible retried on ANY error, so a genuinely intermittent product regression was indistinguishable from the environmental import failure it documented.
Retry budget (3x12s + 25s) exceeded the 60s per-test timeout, so the carefully saved error could never actually be rethrown.
TEST-4's reading-order assertion is tautological when the selector matches 0 or 1 elements; nothing asserted the control count.
TEST-7 sums POST-FIX rendered widths (which the fix itself shrinks by wrapping labels), so it constrains the implementation rather than the property.
measureReach ignores containing-block semantics for absolutely-positioned descendants and clip-path/border-radius.
Every test drove the VIEWPORT, so the primitive's motivating case — a narrow CONTAINER at a wide viewport, the reason the rule is content-driven — was untested.
TEST-6 asserted only getComputedStyle(nested).flexWrap === 'wrap' — a restatement of the class just written, and provably insufficient for a single over-wide item.
The agent-facing manifest documented the new primitive as '_No always-required props._', conveying none of its opinionated child normalization.
The documented escape hatch ('set the height on the row via className') does not work — a row-level height cannot reach the [&>*] rules.
Nothing makes the broken hand-rolled pattern hard to reach; no lint flags `footer={<div className="...justify-end...">}`.
CardActions wraps in DOM order while the sibling DialogFooter/AlertDialogFooter stack in REVERSE (primary on top); the order divergence between three sibling action-row primitives was undocumented.
CardActionsProps omits the KitStyleProps intersection every sibling kit primitive carries, and the comment mis-described it as 'style-gated, like CardProps'.
The header's secondary labels keep whitespace-nowrap with no truncate of their own, so at ~320px a single very long server label can still protrude.
[&>*]:py-1 applied to a plain wrapper div grows the wizard footer ~8px at EVERY width, contradicting the primitive's 'inert when it fits' contract.
The [&>*] block encodes 'every child is a 32px default Button' with no opt-out, so a footer holding a Select/Checkbox/Text or an lg action cannot adopt the primitive without editing it.

The '101 call sites' figure that justified an opt-in primitive over fixing CardFooter counts Drawer/Modal footers too; only ~37 are Card footers, ~7 hand-rolled. The remaining Card footers keep the latent trap.
Same starve-the-name header pattern, same directory, untouched — and it is the TERMINAL state of the very card being fixed.
Two (in fact three) further instances of the identical non-wrapping header pattern inside Cards in the same module, all untouched.
data-slot was written BEFORE {...rest}, so a caller could clobber the only selector the row is addressed by.
No reactive store read in a loop/conditional, no hook-order change, no key/reconciliation change; data-*/aria-* still reach the DOM via {...rest}.

Wrapping makes the card taller at narrow widths and estimateMessageHeight was not updated, enlarging the virtualizer's first-pass estimate correction. Self-correcting via ResizeObserver; no user-visible stall.
whitespace-normal alone breaks only at spaces, so a translated label whose longest TOKEN exceeds the line is still clipped by the Card's overflow-hidden.
TEST-8 hardcoded an English-width 60px legibility floor; no `ziee-chat` string appears anywhere in the diff.
The unconditional catch converted either an environmental import failure or a real intermittent product bug into a green run.
